articles.title: Reparto en la medular
articles.standfirst: Con el regreso de Barrios, Simeone vuelve a contar con todos sus mediocentros
articles.summary: Con el regreso de Barrios, Simeone vuelve a contar con todos sus mediocentros
articles.body: El centro del campo del Atlético ha sido uno de los grandes quebraderos de cabeza de Simeone en las últimas temporadas. Las lesiones han obligado al Cholo a recomponer la medular durante grandes fases de los últimos cursos. Este inicio de Liga trajo consigo las lesiones de Barrios y, de nuevo, saltaron las alarmas. Los tres partidos sin el canterano se saldaron con tres triunfos y con la irrupción de Cardoso como alternativa para el centro del campo. La llegada de Hjulmand este verano elevó el nivel de competencia dentro de la medular rojiblanca. El danés llegaba con la vitola de ser uno de los fichajes estrella del curso y, aunque todavía no ha terminado de consolidarse, ya ha dejado muestras del tipo de jugador que es. Su fichaje, unido a la continuidad de Koke y al paso al frente de Cardoso, permite a Simeone ampliar los recursos en el medio. Sin olvidar la figura de Marcos Llorente. Todo ello, a la espera de que Barrios deje definitivamente atrás sus problemas físicos. Hasta el momento, los cuatro centrocampistas se reparten las titularidades en la medular. Koke, Hjulmand y Barrios suman cuatro partidos como titulares cada uno de los ocho que ha disputado el Atlético. El capitán y el danés han participado en todos ellos, mientras que el canterano y Cardoso solo lo han hecho en cinco encuentros. El norteamericano es el que menos veces ha sido titular, con tan solo dos partidos. El otro futbolista que se ha dejado ver en esa demarcación ha sido Llorente. El 14 es un comodín para Simeone. El reparto de minutos es muy similar al de las titularidades. Koke lidera la tabla con 417 minutos sobre el verde. Barrios, pese a haber disputado tan solo cinco partidos, suma 371 minutos, mientras que Hjulmand acumula 355. El danés también ha entendido su rol cuando ha salido desde el banquillo para ayudar a cerrar partidos. Cardoso, con 225 minutos, es el que menos acumula, pero sus actuaciones han sido de mucha calidad. Tras entrar en la segunda mitad en Anoeta, coincidiendo con la victoria rojiblanca, se hizo fuerte ante Osasuna y el Madrid. Simeone puede presumir del nivel de sus centrocampistas. Tres de ellos, cuatro si contamos a Llorente, han estado trabajando bajo sus órdenes durante este parón de selecciones. Hjulmand, por su parte, acumula minutos de calidad con Dinamarca. Junto a ellos, dos futbolistas jóvenes buscan recuperar con sus selecciones el protagonismo que no están pudiendo tener esta temporada. Vargas, con México, y Mendoza, con la Sub-21, quieren aprovechar el parón para recuperar sensaciones. Mientras tanto, el Cholo por fin parece disponer de varios efectivos para repartir minutos y responsabilidades en la medular.

articles.title: Rui Pinto: Hacker who released Man City documents fears for life as he prepares to lose witness protection
articles.summary: Portuguese computer hacker who released documents which helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City set to lose his witness protection despite fears for his life.
articles.body:
The Portuguese computer hacker who released documents which helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City is set to lose his witness protection despite his fears he could be assassinated.

Football Leaks founder Rui Pinto released a tranche of confidential football documents, including emails and financial records relating to the English Premier League side.

In 2018, he shared documents with German magazine Der Spiegel, which used them for investigations into City's finances and alleged breaches of financial fair play rules.

Last week, City were found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, which they have appealed.

Man City confirm appeal against guilty verdict

The computer hacker who tried to take down Man City

What does Man City guilty verdict mean for their squad?

Pinto became part of Portugal's witness protection programme in 2020 after agreeing to co-operate with authorities and provide files obtained through the Football Leaks operation.

He posted on X on Friday , external that the decision to terminate his participation in the programme on 10 October has put him in a "life-threatening situation".

The 37-year-old said it had left him with no alternative but to relocate to an undisclosed location for an indefinite period because of "multiple death threats" and "the serious risk of an assassination attempt".

BBC Sport has approached the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Crimes in Portugal for comment.

Pinto has described himself as a whistleblower, but was convicted in Portugal of offences including illegal access to data and attempted extortion and given a four-year suspended sentence.

He wore a bulletproof vest during his first trial in 2020, which was also subject to heightened security measures.

Earlier this year, he was acquitted in a second trial of 241 counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to a number of sports bodies in Portugal, including Benfica.

On Wednesday, Pinto turned his attention to Fifa president Gianni Infantino , saying he had "become a cancer on football" and should "have no place in the future of the game".

Pinto repeated allegations from 2018 that Infantino intervened to help City and Paris St-Germain avoid financial fair play sanctions from European football's governing body Uefa.

Infantino's position has recently come under increased pressure following controversial plans to sell stakes in the governing body's competitions, such as the World Cup, to private investors.

A statement from Pinto's lawyers released on Friday said the decision to end his participation in the witness protection programme left him at heightened risk, noting legal proceedings stemming from the leaks remained ongoing, including the case against Manchester City.

Pinto has set up a fundraising page to help him "survive this serious situation", which he claims was "created by the Portuguese State".

articles.title: El Dépor cede ante un Oporto superior
articles.standfirst: Amistoso de ambos clubes con muchas bajas. Jensen adelantó al conjunto local y los goles lusos en la segunda parte obra de Sainz y doblete de André Silva
articles.summary: Amistoso de ambos clubes con muchas bajas. Jensen adelantó al conjunto local y los goles lusos en la segunda parte obra de Sainz y doblete de André Silva
articles.body: El Deportivo recibió este viernes al Oporto en un amistoso. El parón de selecciones ha vaciado los vestuarios de ambos equipos, pero enfrente habrá dos conjuntos de Primera, que fueron rivales en Champions, competición en la que está inmerso el conjunto luso. Riazor se divirtió con cuatro goles y varias acciones que aplaudieron. Francesco Farioli no tenía muchos efectivos del primer equipo (más de diez bajas) pero jugadores como André Silva o Borja Sainz, autores de los goles, son titulares y demostraron su calidad. Se adelantó el Dépor en el inicio de la primera parte en el estreno goleador de Asp Jensen. El Dépor durante los primeros cuarenta y cinco minutos se le vio fresco con Villares y Mario Soriano dirigiendo al equipo en la medular. Por parte visitante un bullicioso y con mucha calidad Alan Varela lo intentaba por todo el frente de ataque. Pero se topó con el poste. La calidad lusa era superior y poco a poco la balanza se inclinaba a favor de los visitantes. Jugadores como Yeremay, Angeliño, Adama o el propio Noé que regresa de una lesión tuvieron minutos para adquirir ritmo de competición. En líneas generales al conjunto de Antonio Hidalgo le sirvió para cargar de minutos a jugadores clave. En el inicio de la segunda mitad empató Sainz. En un mano a mano picó con calidad en la salida de Ferllo. Vendría después el doblete de André Silva, el último gol de bella factura desde el borde del área una volea inalcanzable para Álvaro Ferllo. articles.title: El Racing incluye el nombre de sus abonados en la tercera equipación
articles.standfirst: Incluye en su parte interior los nombres de los 18.804 abonados del club
articles.summary: Incluye en su parte interior los nombres de los 18.804 abonados del club
articles.body: El Racing de Santander ha hecho pública su tercera equipación para la temporada 2026/27, una camiseta negra confeccionada por la marca Austral que incluye en su parte interior los nombres de los 18.804 abonados del club. La camiseta, que el Racing presenta como un homenaje a su afición en el año de su regreso a Primera División 14 años después, incorpora una gráfica tonal inspirada en el lábaro cántabro y detalles en verde en el cuello, los puños y el bajo de la prenda, según informa el club en un comunicado. Así, la tercera equipación se completa con pantalón verde y medias negras con vuelta verde y está confeccionada con tejido técnico 'Quick Dry'. La elástica está disponible a través de la tienda en línea del club por 74,95 euros y, más tarde, también podrá adquirirse en el establecimiento que Tienda Racing tiene en los Campos de Sport de El Sardinero.

articles.title: Punto final a la guerra entre Mbappé y el PSG
articles.standfirst: La justicia francesa archiva la denuncia del 10 blanco contra el club parisino por acoso moral al considerar que no existían pruebas suficientes para continuar
articles.summary: La justicia francesa archiva la denuncia del 10 blanco contra el club parisino por acoso moral
articles.body: La justicia francesa ha archivado la denuncia que Kylian Mbappé presentó contra el PSG por supuesto acoso moral durante su última etapa en el club. La investigación, abierta después de que los abogados del futbolista acudieran a los tribunales, quedó finalmente cerrada en mayo por falta de pruebas suficientes y después de que el propio jugador retirara la denuncia, según informan medios franceses. El origen del caso se remonta al verano de 2023, cuando Mbappé fue apartado del primer equipo del PSG después de comunicar su decisión de no renovar su contrato. El club entendía que el jugador debía renovar o abandonar la entidad a cambio de una importante cantidad de dinero antes de que su vínculo contractual terminara y pudiera marcharse libre. Durante varias semanas, Mbappé quedó al margen de la primera plantilla. Finalmente, fue reintegrado al grupo y pudo volver a competir bajo las órdenes de Luis Enrique, que afrontaba entonces su primera temporada al frente del equipo. El episodio deportivo terminó convirtiéndose también en una batalla judicial. Tras abandonar el PSG al término de aquella temporada para incorporarse al Real Madrid, el club retuvo parte del salario y de las primas que correspondían al futbolista. El PSG sostenía que esas cantidades estaban vinculadas a un acuerdo verbal alcanzado entre Mbappé y el presidente de la entidad, Nasser Al-Khelaifi, que habría permitido su regreso al primer equipo. El jugador rechazó esa interpretación y reclamó las cantidades pendientes. En mayo de 2025 puso en marcha una ofensiva judicial en varios frentes, entre ellos la denuncia por acoso moral relacionada con su apartamiento del equipo. Sin embargo, esa denuncia fue posteriormente retirada por el propio futbolista. La investigación continuó durante un tiempo, pero los jueces instructores terminaron archivándola ante la imposibilidad de seguir adelante con un procedimiento que ya no contaba con el respaldo del denunciante y ante la falta de pruebas suficientes. El otro gran frente judicial, el relacionado con las cantidades económicas que el PSG había retenido, terminó con una resolución favorable a Mbappé. Un Tribunal de lo Laboral obligó al club parisino a abonarle 61 millones de euros. El PSG decidió no recurrir aquella resolución, por lo que la decisión adquirió carácter definitivo. Con el archivo de la denuncia por acoso moral, quedan cerrados los litigios judiciales que enfrentaban a Mbappé con el PSG.

articles.title: LaLiga Futures: el Madrid hace pleno, Orlando y River sorprenden y el Barça al borde de ser eliminado
articles.standfirst: La primera jornada de la X edición Internacional deja grandes partidos y muchas sorpresas
articles.summary: La primera jornada de la X edición Internacional deja grandes partidos y muchas sorpresas
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha arrancado la X edición de LaLIga Futures con puño de hierro. El equipo blanco ha sido el único que jugando dos partidos ha hecho pleno y ya ha logrado la clasificación matemática para los cuartos de final que se disputará en la jornada del sábado en Orlando. El equipo blanco ha ganado al Getafe por la mínima en su debut y al elche con algo más de solvencia en el partido que cerraba la jornada. Le queda el partido contra el Atlético de Madrid mañana en el que no se juega nada. Por su parte los colchoneros suman cuatro puntos y un empate en el derbi les valdría para seguir adelante. En el otro grupo de la muerte, Sevilla y Betis han hecho los deberes y suman cuatro puntos. Con un empate en el derbi andaluz de mañana les daría a ambos para seguir adelante y dejar en la cuenta al Villarreal y al Barcelona que no han competido a su habitual nivel y necesitan ayuda para clasificarse. En los grupos de los equipos internacionales destaca el papel del Orlando que ganó y debe esperar a que River no le gane a Palmeiras para seguir vivo en el torneo. En el último grupo Flamengo es el gran favorito. Boca tiene opciones y el partido entre ambos para dirimir los que siguen adelante será espectacular. La jornada de mañana determinará los cruces de los cuartos de final en la sesión matinal y los mismos darán los semifinalistas en la sesión de tarde.

articles.title: España - República Checa: horario y dónde ver en TV el partido de Nations League
articles.standfirst: Se enfrentan en la tercera jornada de competición
articles.summary: Se enfrentan en la tercera jornada de competición
articles.body: La selección española afronta la tercera jornada de la UEFA Nations League 2026/27 en un gran momento de forma, después de haber conseguido dos victorias en sus dos primeros compromisos. El combinado dirigido por Luis de la Fuente se impuso por 2-3 a Inglaterra en Wembley durante su debut y posteriormente firmó una contundente victoria por 4-1 ante Croacia, con un doblete de Lamine Yamal y tantos de Marc Pubill y Nico Williams. Con seis puntos y el liderato del Grupo A3, España buscará prolongar su excelente dinámica ante su afición y dar un paso más hacia la clasificación para los cuartos de final. Sin embargo, el seleccionador deberá afrontar el encuentro con algunas ausencias importantes, entre ellas las de Nico Williams y Ferran Torres, este último por molestias en el tobillo. Por su parte, la República Checa visita Oviedo con la necesidad de conseguir un resultado positivo para mantener vivas sus aspiraciones en el grupo. El combinado dirigido por Santi Denia ha comenzado la competición con dos derrotas consecutivas, tras caer por 1-2 ante Croacia y por 0-2 frente a Inglaterra. Sin puntos en su casillero, los checos afrontan un desafío de máxima exigencia ante una selección española que atraviesa un gran momento de juego. La disciplina táctica, la solidez defensiva y la capacidad para aprovechar las oportunidades serán fundamentales para intentar sorprender a los actuales líderes del grupo. El conjunto centroeuropeo tratará de romper su mala dinámica y conseguir sus primeros puntos en una competición en la que cada encuentro resulta determinante para sus opciones de permanencia y clasificación. El encuentro correspondiente a la Jornada 3 de la fase de grupos de la UEFA Nations League 2026/27 se disputa mañana, sábado 3 de octubre de 2026, a las 20:45 horas (hora peninsular española), en el estadio Carlos Tartiere de Oviedo. El partido de la Liga de Naciones se podrá seguir en directo y en abierto en España a través de La 1 de TVE y RTVE Play. Además, para no perderte ningún detalle de la previa, conocer las alineaciones oficiales de ambos conjuntos y disfrutar de las reacciones y el análisis posterior, podrás seguir la cobertura online en MARCA y otros medios deportivos, así como la retransmisión radiofónica de Radio MARCA.

articles.title: El Eldense remonta y se estrena en el Pepico Amat... a penalti limpio
articles.standfirst: Dos penas máximas en apenas 12 minutos marcadas por Roberto López y Fidel voltean el gol de Reina, el más rápido de LaLiga, y Olabarrieta y Rastrojo sentencian
articles.summary: Dos penas máximas en apenas 12 minutos marcadas por Roberto López y Fidel voltean el gol de Reina, el más rápido de LaLiga, y Olabarrieta y Rastrojo sentencian
articles.body: Con dos penaltis a favor en apenas 12 minutos y los postreros goles de Olabarrieta y Rastrojo el Eldense del nuevo propietario Leo Messi no sólo remontó el tempranero gol de Reina para el Oviedo, sino que consigue su primera victoria en el Nuevo Pepico Amat y sale provisionalmente de los puestos de descenso. Por contra, el cuadro carbayón no pudo encadenar dos triunfos por primera vez esta temporada y sufre su tercera derrota. Buscaba el Eldense refrendar en casa las sensaciones que transmitía pero sin hacerlas efectivas en forma de puntos, a la vez que el Oviedo llegaba con un chute de adrenalina tras vencer el derbi ante el Sporting. Javi Calleja y Julián Calero buscaban por dónde remendar las costuras sobre el tapete con bajas en ambas escuadras. En los locales, la medular con la baja se Justin y una delantera entre algodones una semana más y con poca artillería; y en los asturianos, más de lo mismo con rotaciones bajo palos y en punta. El inicio premió a los carbayones a los 19 segundos, gol eléctrico de una acción de banda a banda que, con otra desconexión en la zaga local, David Jiménez paseó un balón que Reina mandó a la red. Golpe severo para el Eldense que sufrió para reponerse de ello, aunque reaccionó pronto, con alguna internada de Fidel en banda y con un potente disparo de Macho que sacó con seguridad y junto al larguero el debutante Narváez, mientras Manu Nieto mandó al limbo desde el área pequeña y con todo a favor un córner prolongado de cabeza. Entre medias el ex local Youness rondó el 0-2, pero su cabezazo cruzado tras un córner de Goti se fue algo desviado. De nuevo estuvo muy acertado el joven Narváez al sacar el potente disparo de Guirao y justo antes del descanso Fidel tuvo una falta en la frontal del área grande, pero la estrelló en la barrera. El Eldense nunca encontró sensaciones más allá de intentar gestionar el balón sin éxito sobre el área asturiana. En la segunda mitad probó Calleja a permutar de salida con Larios y Roberto López y encontrar algo de luz entre la zaga de Calero. A base de insistir en banda derecha, una internada de Ibarrondo acabó en una clara mano de Samu que el árbitro Rafael Sánchez López castigó con penalti y Roberto López lo aprovechó para empatar... antes de caer lesionado. El Eldense creyó y el Oviedo ya no encontró la misma comodidad y a renglón seguido el propio Ibarrondo tuvo el segundo pero, con todo a favor, tras gran cesión de Waldo, no fue capaz de superar a Narváez. El que sí logró voltear el marcador fue Fidel, al marcar un segundo penalti, éste por un ligero agarrón de Pablo Sáenz a Larios cuando su compañero Roberto López se había tenido que marchar lesionado. Intentó sentenciar un Eldense superior, pero Narváez le negó el gol a Olabarrieta. Lo intentó el Oviedo hasta el final, pero la ocasión de Jacobo la sacó tirándose al suelo un Ramón Vila casi inédito la segunda parte. Y de tanto volcarse el equipo carbayón en el añadido Olabarrieta sentenció a pase de Bustillo tras un error de Aisar en una contra fulgurante y Rastrojo, con una gran picadita tras robarle el balón a Aisar, culminó la goleada en otro contragolpe. Tácticamente, el Eldense impuso su estilo que acabó por premiarle tras varias partidos sin dicha fortuna. Alberto Reina abrió el marcador en el Nuevo Pepico Amat muy pronto, de hecho lo hizo con el gol más rápido de la temporada en LaLiga Hypermotion, en concreto a los 19 segundos, superando así el de Álex Rubio a los 30’’ en el Albacete-Córdoba de la sexta jornada.

articles.title: El Aston Villa de Emery se hace con el XV Trofeo Antonio Puerta
articles.standfirst: Barkley, Garnacho y Jenner anularon la ventaja del gol de Isaac Romero
articles.summary: Barkley, Garnacho y Jenner anularon la ventaja del gol de Isaac Romero
articles.body: El Aston Villa se adjudicó el XV Trofeo Antonio Puerta tras remontar con goles de Barkley, Garnacho y Jenner el tanto inicial de Isaac Romero. Unai Emery regresaba a Nervión, la que fue su casa entre enero de 2013 y junio de 2016, y de donde salió con la maleta repleta de títulos: tres UEFA Europa League consecutivas. El vasco pisaba el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán al frente del Aston Villa para recordar la figura de la 'Zurda de Diamantes'. Los tres trofeos presidieron, junto a Jesús Navas, Coke, Diogo, Javi Varas, Negredo, Fazio, Nico Pareja, Sergio Rico y Vicente Iborra, el homenaje al técnico en el césped. Con la ausencia de un buen número de internacionales en ambos bandos, tiempo para evaluar a los menos habituales, para hacer probaturas y también para una nueva lesión de Marcao en un encuentro con ritmo pese a la condición de amistoso. Un examen de altura para los andaluces ante un equipo Champions. Apuntamos la primera a un latigazo de Buendía. El disparo del argentino dio con la pelota en el techo de la portería de Fran González. El guardameta, que abandonó la concentración de la sub 21 por unas molestias, estrenó titularidad al igual que Marcao. Replicó Manu Bueno con un disparo centrado, y blandito, tras uno de los chispazos de Ejuke por la banda izquierda que detuvo sin problemas Bizot. A partir de ahí se estiró el Sevilla con el nigeriano monopolizando el juego de las bandas blanquirrojas hasta que Alfon también se metió en la película. La más clara para los villanos estuvo en las botas de Tammy Abraham. Se plantó bien Fran González en una rápida acción del Aston Villa, se hizo grande en el uno contra uno y despejó el remate del delantero. Después entraría el polivalente Juan Iglesias para jugar de central tras la lesión de Marcao. Ejuke remató ligeramente desviado una jugada que comenzó con un caño de Alfon desde la derecha, Peque aguantó y cedió el balón para el disparo con veneno del nigeriano. Lo intentaría el catalán tras un buen pase de Isaac. Encimado por los dos centrales visitantes, remató muy alto aunque pidió córner. Un disparo desviado de Buendía y poco más que contar antes de marcharse los jugadores a vestuarios. Qué mejor homenaje para Antonio Puerta que un canterano abriese el marcador con el '16' en la espalda. Los sevillistas salieron como un tiro tras el receso y con Fofana en el césped por Agoumé. Volcados en la portería de Bizot, Isaac Romero estuvo atento para cazar un balón suelto en el área, tras un disparo de Peque bloqueado por un defensor, y abrir el marcador con un trallazo. Tras el gol se hizo con el balón el Aston Villa. Fran González repelió un disparo alto de Hemmings y lo intentó en varias ocasiones Garnacho, que más adelante tendría su premio. Los errores pusieron al Sevilla a los pies de los caballos. Barkley igualó el marcador y pudo poner por delante a los ingleses. Un fallo en la entrega del canterano Mario Díaz, que midió mal el pase de Fofana, propició el robo del '6', que no perdonó. Un remate posterior se marchó desviado tras otra pérdida, en este caso de Guridi. El carrusel de cambios no le sentó igual a los equipos. Tampoco el fondo de armario es el mismo. Garnacho, que se cambió de banda, remató completamente solo un balón en el segundo palo. Jenner amplió la distancia en el marcador tras adentrarse en el área en velocidad y definir ante Fran González por abajo. articles.standfirst: El mito bosnio se retiró de la Selección tras salir del campo en el minuto 61 del choque
articles.summary: El mito bosnio se retiró de la Selección tras salir del campo en el minuto 61 del choque
articles.body: Se acabó la historia de Edin Dzeko (a sus 40 años) en Bosnia y Herzegovina. El delantero del Schalke colgó la camiseta de su país en el empate de esta noche ante Suecia (1-1). Fue emotiva, pero algo triste, pues el gol de Gyokeres echó por tierra la emoción de despedir al mejor jugador en la historia del país. Luego, eso sí, lo arregló un poco Alajbegovic en el 80' con el tanto del empate (1-1). Recordemos que Dzeko debutó en junio de 2007 con la Selección (marcó ese día) y se va con 152 partidos jugados y 73 tantos celebrados. Jugó las Copas del Mundo de 2014 y 2026. El ariete no pudo celebrar ningún tanto, pero a punto estuvo, pues su gol en el 45+2 fue anulado por haber salido la pelota fuera del terreno de juego en la jugada anterior. Una pena. Antes del partido, y cuando llegó el minuto 11, los hinchas bosnios le demostraron cariño a Edin con abundante pirotecnia desde los edificios colindantes al estadio. Finalmente, y con 0-1 en el marcador, se retiró del campo en el minuto 63', sustituido por Tabakovic. El homenaje se alargó tras el partido.

articles.title: De Bruyne, con un doblete, protagoniza otra pesadilla turca
articles.standfirst: Güler, con doble amarilla, se perderá el duelo ante Italia y podría regresar antes a Madrid
articles.summary: El doblete del belga y el tanto de Lukaku sentencian a una Turquía que vuelve a tropezar. Güler lo intentó, pero fue insuficiente
articles.body: Cuando enciendes la televisión para ver un partido de Turquía, últimamente parece que estás viendo siempre el mismo culebrón. Esta vez, sin embargo, el protagonista fue Kevin De Bruyne, autor de un doblete que terminó por hundir a los otomanos. Francia e Italia habían dejado a los de Montella tocados ante su público (con pitos incluidos) y el partido ante Bélgica se presentaba como una oportunidad para cambiar el rumbo. La reacción empezaba por el once. Toque de atención o no, el técnico italiano modificó la alineación con hasta seis cambios. Çakir regresaba a la portería tras cumplir sanción y la medular también era inédita, con Yüksek y Elmaz formando pareja. Van Bommel, en cambio, agitó menos el árbol, con tres cambios para buscar otra versión belga. Esa versión llegó acompañada de un tempranero golazo de Kevin De Bruyne en el 10', que volvió a recordar al futbolista que tantas veces encontraba la red bajo las órdenes de Guardiola. Los problemas turcos no hacían más que aumentar. El gol les sentó mal y De Ketelaere y Lukébakio probaron suerte, sin encontrar el segundo. En el desconcierto turco apareció su estrella. Arda Güler asumió responsabilidades y se echó el equipo a la espalda. De sus botas nacieron las mejores ocasiones, aunque una y otra vez se topó con Lammers. No solo con disparos, también con centros. Con su 'guante' encontró a Bardakci, pero el desenlace volvió a ser el mismo: Lammers. Cierto es que el madridista pecó de individualista en alguna llegada, pero es lo único diferencial que tiene Turquía. El arreón duró poco. Los 'Diablos Rojos' volvieron a la carga y tuvieron dos ocasiones clarísimas para doblar la ventaja. Primero fue Vanaken, con un taconazo, y después Lukébakio, en un mano a mano que Cakir salvó con la yema de los dedos para mandar el balón a la madera. En la última del primer tiempo, Demiral se encontró con un balón muerto dentro del área. Sólo, con todo a favor, incomprensiblemente lo mandó a las nubes. Los segundos 45' arrancaron frenéticos, con tres ocasiones claras en apenas tres minutos. Kadioglu probó desde lejos y, en la réplica, Lukébakio encaró al propio lateral para volver a encontrarse con la madera. Sin tiempo para respirar, Turquía volvió a rondar la portería belga con Akgün, recién incorporado, pero de nuevo apareció Lammers. En ese intercambio de golpes, Bélgica volvió a golpear. Otra vez Kevin De Bruyne, con un latigazo en el 59', para firmar el segundo y hundir más a los otomanos. En el 76', otro despiste de la zaga turca terminó de sentenciarles. Los belgas sacaron rápido una falta, encontraron a De Ketelaere y el atacante asistió a Lukaku, que puso el 3-0. Desde entonces, no hubo más. La única amenaza llegó de las botas de Güler, con un lanzamiento de falta que despejó el guardameta. Turquía se encontró con otra pesadilla, esta vez protagonizada por De Bruyne, que agranda todavía más sus problemas. Bélgica, segunda de grupo con seis puntos, visitará ahora a Francia con dos bajas de peso: De Bruyne y Tielemans.

articles.title: Olise no basta ante una Italia con fe y un Donnarumma imperial
articles.standfirst: Primer tropiezo de la era Zidane en casa después de que Bastoni igualara la maravilla de falta del atacante del Bayern y el arquero del City firmara una noche estelar
articles.summary: Primer tropiezo de la era Zidane en casa después de que Bastoni igualara la maravilla de falta del atacante del Bayern y el arquero del City firmara una noche estelar
articles.body: Zidane patinó en su retorno a casa. Ni la obra de arte de Olise bastó para mantener el pleno del técnico francés. Dominaron la posesión y el juego, pero Bastoni neutralizó el tanto local y Donnarumma se erigió en un gigante insuperable bajo palos, amargando la noche a una Francia que se desesperó ante el entramado italiano. Aparentemente, Francia siempre mandó con holgura. Acaparaba casi un 20 % más de posesión e instalada en campo contrario, pero le faltaba ese vértigo que tan bien maneja Mbappé. Doué, Olise y Cherki llegaban con soltura y velocidad a la frontal, pero ahí morían todas sus intenciones. Mucha intensidad y ritmo, pero ni un solo balón claro para Dembélé. Italia, en cambio, vivía cómoda sin la pelota. Mancini ordenó apretar los dientes en la última línea y por allí no pasaba ni el aire. A la contra, los italianos silenciaron el Stade de France. Primero fue Kean, que erró un gol cantado: Kayode, tras un cambio de juego brillante de Frattesi, puso un pase de la muerte al segundo palo para el delantero del Como, pero este no pudo superar a Maignan cuando ya parecía batido. Hizo lo más difícil. La segunda de la Azzurra provocó el murmullo en la grada. En un saque de banda —sí, de banda—, Pio Esposito la bajó de espaldas y la dejó servida para Frattesi, que de manera increíble no acertó entre los tres palos en el área pequeña. En el córner posterior le anularon un gol por claro fuera de juego al propio Kean, desatando definitivamente todas las dudas en el cuadro francés. Tras el descanso cedió el muro y emergió la figura gigante de Donnarumma. El guardameta sostuvo a su selección en pie con un auténtico festival de paradones que minaron el Stade de France. Su estratosférica doble parada a disparos de Olise y Dembélé, sumada a un carrusel de vuelos imposibles para despejar los latigazos de Camavinga, Rabiot y el propio Olise, inyectó de moral a una Italia que adolece de estrellas, pero presenta una convicción de hierro. Ni el mejor Donnarumma pudo hacer nada ante el golazo de Olise. Francia mostró otro talante tras el descanso, más contundente, pero el gol no llegó hasta que la plantó el delantero del Bayern. Su tiro libre fue un latigazo seco que buscó el ángulo izquierdo y toco el larguero antes de entrar para firmar un golazo colosal y llevar la locura al estadio. Se repetía el guion de Bélgica para los de Zizou, pero Italia se resistió a entregarse a pesar del golpe. Mantuvo la compostura atrás, pero adelantó líneas y en una presión insistente se la liaron a los galos. Alessandro Bastoni apareció desde la cueva para robarle la cartera a Da Cunha, que se confió al darse la vuelta tras recibir de Rabiot. El central del Inter le arrebató el cuero con la potencia de un avión y se plantó solo en el área para definir con la solvencia del mejor ariete el mano a mano ante Maignan. Para colmo, la expulsión de Upamecano —fruto de un enganchón y una posterior falta sobre Kean— terminó de minar la moral francesa. Lo intentó sin descanso el retornado Camavinga con disparos lejanos, pero la noche pertenecía a un Donnarumma insuperable que terminó certificando la resistencia italiana.

articles.title: 49ers owner Jed York suspended for 6 games after his arrest in prostitution sting
articles.summary: The NFL suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York for six games Friday following his arrest earlier this year in a prostitution sting in Ohio.
articles.body: The NFL suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York for six games Friday following his arrest earlier this year in a prostitution sting in Ohio. The league announced that York also was fined $500,000 for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. York has not attended any games or league meetings so far this season and was credited with three games served. He is eligible to return on Oct. 20, following the team’s game the previous night against Washington. The NFL’s fall league meetings begin that day in New York. York said in a statement released by the team that he accepts the punishment given by the league and apologized for his actions. “To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry,” he said. “This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one’s failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don’t take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead.” York was arrested in a mobile home park by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force after police said he was attempting to pay $160 for sex with a woman he believed to be a prostitute. York was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. Police seized the $160 from York and that was later given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course. Owners have been previously punished for violating the personal conduct policy. The late Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay was suspended for six games and fined $500,000 following a guilty plea to driving while impaired in 2014. New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was investigated but not punished by the league after he was arrested in Florida in 2019 for allegedly paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. The charge was later dropped after a court ruled that police violated the rights of Kraft and the other customers when they secretly installed video cameras inside massage rooms at the spa. York spent most of the summer in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown and had been away from the team even before his arrest. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records. York took over day-to-day control of the 49ers from his parents in 2008. He became the team’s principal owner in 2024. After some initial struggles under York’s leadership, the team has been a consistent contender since hiring coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch in 2017. The Niners have made the Super Bowl three times under York’s leadership, losing in the 2012 season under coach Jim Harbaugh and the 2019 and ’23 seasons under Shanahan and Lynch. York also oversaw the building of Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara. The team moved from San Francisco to the new stadium in 2014. The stadium has hosted two Super Bowls, a World Cup and a College Football Playoff title game.

articles.title: Yáñez acaba con las desgracias del Castilla y le da una alegría en el derbi
articles.standfirst: El golazo del extremo decide un duelo donde los blancos encajaron dos desafortunados goles y se salvaron del empate tras un remate al larguero del rojiblanco Castillo en el 101'
articles.summary: El golazo del extremo decide un duelo donde los blancos encajaron dos desafortunados goles y se salvaron del empate tras un remate al larguero del rojiblanco Castillo en el 101'
articles.body: Expía sus pecados el equipo de López de Lerma ganando el miniderbi ante su afición y volviendo a recuperar para la causa a un Cestero que dio empaque a la medular de un Castilla que, con Thiago Pitarch, marcó la diferencia. Un gran gol de Yáñez acabó con las desgracias de un filial blanco que encajó dos desafortunados goles, uno en propia puerta de Mario Rivas justo antes del descanso y otro en el rechace de un penalti parado por Mestre, y que cerca estuvo de encajar el 3-3 en el minuto 101 en un remate del rojiblanco Castillo que se estrelló en el larguero. Una montaña rusa de situaciones que acabó con una gran alegría para el Castilla, que coge impulso imponiéndose en el derbi ante el Atlético Madrileño y sale de una mala racha de resultados. El mini derbi disputaba su primer episodio de la temporada en una grada casi llena del Di Stéfano, donde la afición blanca disfrutó de una primera parte en la que los pupilos de López de Lerma ofrecieron un gran poderío ofensivo, aunque no se vio reflejado en el marcador al final de los primeros 45 minutos. Una gran jugada personal de Ángel Carvajal antes del minuto 10 sirvió para poner la ventaja en el luminoso para los locales, que pudo verse ampliada por varias jugadas de mérito de Leiva y de un Thiago Pitarch que quiso dejar su sello en varios momentos en este periplo con el Castilla. Los de Torres supieron aguantar bien para rehacerse con paciencia e ir ganando terreno poco. Pudieron empatar por mediación de Cubo, en un bonito movimiento del delantero que tocando de espuela a punto estuvo de sorprender a Mestre. Pero finalmente fue el lejano disparo de Antal el que se encontró con un despeje poco acertado de Mario Rivas y el cuero se alojó en las mallas. El empate antes del descanso era un hecho, pero el momento de duda madridista a punto estuvo de costarles el segundo gol rojiblanco. Sólo el palo consiguió evitarlo al remate de David García. La segunda parte estuvo marcada por el intercambio de golpes que se inició con los penaltis señalados a favor de cada conjunto. En apenas cinco minutos el marcador y la sensaciones cambiaron de bando. Primero la pena señalada sobre Aguado, que él mismo se encargó de materializar. En la siguiente jugada llegaría el penalti para los rojiblancos, en una internada de Cubo en el área, siendo derribado por Aguado. David García no pudo batir a un Mestre, que repelió el disparo desde el punto de penalti, para que el recién entrado Koke remachara el tanto de la igualada. El choque ganó en viveza buscando ambos poder disolver las tablas. Y tuvo que ser Yáñez con un fenomenal zurdazo en una jugada habitual, el que llevara el delirio a la grada del Di Stéfano a casi veinte minutos para el final. Pol Fortuny a punto estuvo de sellar el resultado con un remate que salió por encima del larguero cuando el choque casi llegaba al 90’. El filial rojiblanco tendría el empate en el minuto 101', cuando Jorge Castillo a punto estuvo de aguar la fiesta blanca con un remate que se estrelló en el larguero y con el que se llegaría al final del partido. articles.title: Former Yale football coach Tony Reno dies at 52, less than 1 year after stepping down due to health issues
articles.summary: Reno is the second-winningest head coach in program history.
articles.body:
Former Yale head football coach Tony Reno has died, the program announced Friday . He was 52.

This past February, Reno stepped down from his post after a 14-season run at the helm due to health reasons. At the time, Yale didn't specify Reno's medical issues.

With an 83-49 record from 2012-25, Reno is the second-winningest head coach in program history. He trails only Carm Cozza, the iconic Bulldogs coach who won 179 games and 10 Ivy League titles amid a tenure that stretched from 1965 to 1996.

"Today, we are deeply saddened by the loss of an extraordinary member of the Yale Athletics family," said Yale athletic director Vicky Chun in a statement. "Tony Reno devoted his life to serving others and approached every day with humility, compassion, and purpose. He believed deeply in the power of mentorship and invested wholeheartedly in the success and well-being of his players, colleagues, and friends. While his accomplishments on the football field were remarkable, it is the relationships he built and the lives he changed that will define his enduring legacy. Our thoughts are with Toni, Dante, Angelina, Vince, and the entire Reno family during this time."

While his accomplishments on the football field were remarkable, it is the relationships he built and the lives he changed that will define his enduring legacy. Our thoughts are with Toni, Dante, Angelina, Vince, and the entire Reno family during this time."

Dante Reno, a son of Tony, is currently in his second season as the Bulldogs' starting quarterback. During Dante's first go-around as QB1, a 2025 campaign that wound up being his father's final season as head coach, he threw for 21 touchdowns, and Yale notched its first FCS playoff victory — in comeback fashion, no less.

After facing a 35-7 halftime deficit, the Renos and the rest of the Bulldogs rallied for a jaw-dropping win, 43-42, over Youngstown State.

The 2025 season marked the first time that Ivy League teams could vie for an FCS national championship. So when Tony Reno collected his fifth Ivy League title, it also came with a spot in the FCS playoffs, setting the stage for that epic mid-game turnaround.

Reno's Bulldogs also wore the Ivy crown in 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2023. They finished with a winning record in six of his final eight seasons with the program. Plus, he won seven of his last nine meetings versus rival Harvard. In that span, the Bulldogs emerged victorious from a 50-43 double-overtime game in 2019.

A Massachusetts native, Reno put down roots in New Haven, Connecticut, where he spent formative years as a Yale assistant in the 2000s. After a stint as Harvard's special teams coordinator and defensive backs coach, he returned to take the Bulldogs' head job.

He stayed put, while earning an array of accolades along the way. In 2022, he was named Ivy League Coach of the Year. That season, his Bulldogs went 8-2, including 6-1 in the Ivy.

But Reno left a legacy larger than any record or award can signify, as explained in a statement from current Yale head coach Kevin Cahill.

"Tony was a man who valued the important things in life," said Cahill, who coached under Reno from 2012-22 before rebuilding Lehigh into an FCS power from 2023-25. "Family always came first, and that was evident in the special family he built and the love the Reno family shares. As a coach, Tony loved his players and held them to a standard they often didn't know they were capable of reaching. He was hard on them and demanding, but every day, they knew he cared about them. It was never about him or simply about winning championships; it was about developing young men and leaders and helping them become the best versions of themselves."

articles.title: Ukraine 0-3 Northern Ireland: Ciaron Brown scores first international goals with Isaac Price also on target in Nations League win
articles.summary: Match report as Michael O'Neill's side cruise to a dominant victory over Ukraine in Slovakia; Ciaron Brown scores either side of Isaac Price's strike as Northern Ireland go top of Nations League Group B2
articles.body:
Brown, the only player in Michael O'Neill's starting line-up over the age of 24, scrambled in early on before Isaac Price doubled the lead in the 22nd minute at the Stadion Antona Malatinskeho in Trnava, Slovakia.

Brown's second then came in bizarre fashion just after the hour - the 28-year-old Oxford defender went up to flick on Pierce Charles' free-kick from inside the Northern Ireland half and Ukraine goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk let the bouncing ball through his legs.

On paper this was the hardest game in the group, away to a side ranked 37 places above Northern Ireland, but they brushed Ukraine aside to move on to seven points from their opening three games since returning to their second tier, still yet to concede going into Monday's game with Georgia in Belfast.

This was the first competitive meeting with Ukraine since Northern Ireland's famous 2-0 win at Euro 2016, and they delivered a performance which will have fans believing a major tournament beckons for this new generation.

O'Neill made three changes from Monday's goalless draw against Hungary - one enforced with Ethan Galbraith one of two players, Callum Marshall the other, absent for personal reasons.

Justin Devenny and Patrick Kelly also dropped out as Brodie Spencer, Terry Devlin and teenager Kieran Morrison came in, with the 19-year-old Morrison, on loan at Sheffield Wednesday from Liverpool, helping to bring the average age down to a flat 22, Northern Ireland's youngest post-war starting XI.

A positive start from Northern Ireland was quickly rewarded as Morrison floated a corner to the back post where Ruairi McConville headed it back for Brown, earning his 33rd cap, to prod home despite the desperate efforts of Illia Zabarnyi on the line.

Ukraine bossed the ball but struggled to break down Northern Ireland. Georgiy Sudakov was the first to get a sight of goal but his 19th-minute effort was straight at Charles.

Moments later Northern Ireland doubled their lead. As they countered, Morrison's first-time ball into the box was met powerfully by Price at the back post - giving Morrison an assist in his first competitive international.

Charles clawed away a powerful strike from Eduard Sarapii, but although Northern Ireland were needing to do a lot of defending, a Ukraine side sporting 10 changes for a second straight match created few clear chances.

Mykola Matviyenko threatened less than two minutes after the restart but that was a false dawn for the hosts, who found themselves three down thanks to Riznyk's horror moment in the 61st minute, with Brown's header trickling over the line.

Ukraine substitute Matvii Ponomarenko hit the outside of the post but a shellshocked Ukraine side rarely looked like getting back into it.

Late on Ceadach O'Neill came off the bench to make his fourth Northern Ireland appearance, ending any discussion of a possible switch to the Republic of Ireland for the Arsenal teenager.

articles.title: Ukraine 0-3 Northern Ireland: Who has 'no ceiling' as Michael O'Neill's side shine?
articles.summary: After an impressive 3-0 victory over Ukraine in the Nations League, Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill was impressed with his young side.
articles.body:
Michael O'Neill had spent the build-up to Northern Ireland's Nations League outing against Ukraine playing down memories of their famous win at Euro 2016.

His focus was firmly on what was to come rather than reflect on the past.

If a stunning 3-0 victory on Friday night was anything to go by, it's going to be a pretty exciting future indeed.

His starting team had an average age of just 22, which was the youngest on record for Northern Ireland since World War Two.

Oxford's Ciaron Brown, the only player over the age of 25 to start the game in Trnava, Slovakia, was in the right place to open the scoring in the ninth minute from Ruairi McConville's knockdown.

O'Neill handed a first start to 19-year-old Kieran Morrison, and his superb cross led to Isaac Price doubling the lead, before Brown's header evaded goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk in bizarre circumstances with 30 minutes left.

While the victory may not be quite as memorable as the 2-0 'Kings of Lyon' success 10 years ago at the Euros, it was extremely impressive.

To put it into context - and never mind the manner of the performance - only Sweden and France have beaten Ukraine in the past 12 months.

Northern Ireland can now be added to that list.

Brown scores two as superb Northern Ireland stun Ukraine

Inside Northern Ireland's football conveyor belt

Brown's two goals were just reward for a player who has been quietly impressive for far longer than this campaign, and he was part of a back-five which stood out in what was a third consecutive clean sheet.

Brodie Spencer and Terry Devlin were drafted in at the full-back positions and both impressed, but Brown's centre-back partners McConville and Tom Atcheson really shone.

Norwich City defender McConville, 21, commanded his area well and, as well as an assist for Brown, he also allowed the ball to trickle over the line when he could have touched home for the third goal instead of his team-mate.

Atcheson, himself only 20 and playing for Blackburn Rovers in the Championship, made his Northern Ireland debut in Wales in March, but showed composure beyond his years.

O'Neill said both players were "terrific" as he told BBC Sport: "They have no ceiling, to be honest.

"They are both playing in the Championship at the minute but they are ready to go to the next level.

"They will make mistakes at times and we've put a lot on them in terms of the physicality. The two of them were brilliant."

O'Neill was also delighted for Brown, who said he had "really grown" into a senior role in the absence of injured Sunderland defender Dan Ballard.

"Three 90 minutes at this level is tough," said O'Neill of the 28-year-old.

"He plays his club football in League One and he's a better player than that.

"He brings a lot to the team. He was our most senior player tonight and he has really grown into that."

When asked what was the most pleasing aspect of a positive night, O'Neill added it was the "overall performance".

"We played a really good team tonight and we had to be really well set-up," he said.

"The team was really well prepared and the staff done an amazing job, from the analysis to the set-pieces and right through everything.

"Everything fell into place a little bit, we scored early from a set-piece and the second goal was brilliant.

"Another clean sheet and there were some really good performances right through the squad."

With four goals scored and none conceded, O'Neill's side are in great shape at the halfway point of the campaign.

They are three points clear of Hungary and Ukraine at the top of League B2, and host a Georgia side - who have one solitary point to date - back at Windsor Park on Monday night.

If they can end the quadruple-header unbeaten they will head into November's final two matches on a high, and the wider implications are significant.

Topping the group would seal promotion to League A for the first time, and mean Northern Ireland will be in a five-team group for Euro 2028 qualification, with a potential fall-back of a play-off should the campaign go awry.

They had not won an away Nations League match before Shea Charles' 99th-minute winner in Georgia, and this was their biggest away success in five years.

Former international Stephen Craigan, on co-commentary in Slovakia, described it as potentially "a seismic night" for a young group, which was missing Ballard, the influential Ethan Galbraith and Liverpool defender Conor Bradley, while Justin Devenny started on the bench.

The real implications of the victory may only become clear further down the line, but all focus for now will be on the recovery before the final game of the window on Monday.

"There is a big togetherness in a young group," said the 23-year-old Price, who scored his first international goal in just over a year.

"We're loving it and we love coming away. It's about building momentum and we're doing that."

articles.title: Unai Emery, tras su regreso a Nervión: "Me siento muy querido"
articles.standfirst: El Aston Villa se proclama campeón del XV Trofeo Antonio Puerta
articles.summary: El Aston Villa se proclama campeón del XV Trofeo Antonio Puerta
articles.body: Unai Emery regresó al Sánchez-Pizjuán para disputar con el Aston Villa el Trofeo Antonio Puerta. Los ingleses se proclamaron campeones de esta XV edición del torneo tras remontar el tanto de Isaac Romero. El técnico, que dejó una huella imborrable en Nervión tras logras tres UEFA Europa League de manera consecutiva, fue homenajeado en el césped en la previa del encuentro frente al conjunto hispalense. "Sevilla me enseñó muchas cosas, me hizo mejor entrenador, me hizo mejor persona. Luego he venido poco porque he estado prácticamente trabajando. Venir un día como hoy para mí es muy importante. Las anteriores que he venido ha sido jugando con el Villarreal y no tienes más tiempo más que para estar concentrado con tu equipo. Vine, por desgracia, a lo de Reyes. Estuve aquí dos días y uno vuelve a recordar muchas cosas, sobre todo desde lo que suponía Reyes también para mí personalmente. Y venir hoy, con el trofeo Antonio Puerta, para mí es un día también especial", comenzaba el técnico en los medios oficiales del club blanquirrojo. "Es un partido amistoso, pero tratas de darle seriedad y también cosas que quieres para tu equipo. Ha sido un día muy bonito porque me han sorprendido con la presencia de los trofeos y de los jugadores, que ha sido magnífico. Considero que dentro de lo que es el fútbol, el ganar, el perder, los momentos buenos, momentos malos, yo me siento muy querido y a la vez quiero a mucha gente de aquí", continuaba. "Esperaba hoy que el campo tuviese una presencia masiva de aficionados y así ha sido. Ha sido revivir en pocos minutos grandes momentos que hemos tenido aquí. Ver jugadores que me demostraron una lealtad al Sevilla, al trabajo, al entrenador, compromiso para trabajar todo lo que le dedicábamos y conseguir al final los objetivos más o menos que planteábamos. Para mí siempre me sentiré muy orgulloso. La relación entre jugadores y entrenadores siempre tiene sus dificultades, pero cuando la cosa colectivamente tiene un beneficio para el Sevilla, los aficionados, los técnicos, para los jugadores, todo explota desde lo positivo y desde la alegría. Estar aquí, hoy, en estas fechas, con este calor, me hace recordar lo bueno que tiene Sevilla", bromeó el vasco. Por último señalaba: "Nosotros también teníamos objetivos colectivos e individuales con los jugadores que menos están jugando y queríamos darle seriedad al partido. Los jugadores han dado esa seriedad y, aunque el resultado no sea importante en un partido amistoso, competir y mantener esa mentalidad siempre viene bien. Ha sido un día completo a nivel profesional, por lo que queríamos conseguir, y también completo por vivir este momento y recordar muchas cosas".

articles.title: England 0-0 Slovakia: U21s book their spot at Euro 2027 with Stoke stalemate
articles.summary: Match report as England U21s qualify for Euro 2027 after draw with Slovakia in Stoke; Lee Carsley's side only needed a point to send them through to next summer's European Championship, which is being held in Albania and Serbia
articles.body:
The Young Lions sat six points ahead of Slovakia before their meeting, with two games remaining, which meant Lee Carsley's side only needed a draw to send them through to Euro 2027.

Carsley said his side would go for the win but were frustrated by a Slovakia team that sat with a low block.

England came closest through Will Lankshear, who nodded wide a couple of headers in the first period, but they seemed content to take a point and qualify for a tournament they are looking to win for a third successive time.

England were the only side looking for an opener. Sydie Peck picked out the in-form Lankshear who guided a header wide and Ethan Nwaneri also came close.

Along came another chance for Lankshear, this time assisted by the bright Tyrique George, but the Middlesbrough striker narrowly nodded wide of the far post.

Chelsea's Josh Acheampong scored last Friday night and he tested the palms of Adam Hrdina from range to make his first save.

Slovakia needed a goal to keep their faint chances of automatic qualification open, and started the second period with a bit more intensity than the first. Hugo Pavek had a crack from long range which James Beadle needed to be alert to.

Samuel Amo-Ameyaw looked menacing and was particularly causing problems for Slovakia full-back Filip Mielke. He fashioned himself an opportunity early in the second half by cutting inside but aimed over the crossbar.

England continued to look for a goal that would break the deadlock. Archie Gray tried his luck from range to see if he could mark the occasion with a goal but Slovakia's defence stood strong.

Amario Cozier-Duberry replaced George but right-back Pavek's evening did not get any easier, this time the Middlesbrough winger cut inside and flashed in a cross for Peck who could not guide home the opener as both sides settled for a point.

articles.title: Kentucky appeals court dissolves injunction that granted 38 players, including Thomas Castellanos, Seth Trimble and Mark Mitchell, a fifth year of eligibility
articles.summary: The ruling further exemplifies the chaos surrounding the NCAA's five-for-five implementation.
articles.body:
Could quarterback Thomas Castellanos' time at Texas Tech already be over?

On Friday, the Kentucky Court of Appeals ruled against athletes from the class of 2022 who had been granted a fifth year of eligibility via a temporary injunction. According to On3 , a hearing is scheduled in the matter for Oct. 9 as the lawsuit is still pending.

Castellanos was part of a group of players who had successfully been granted a fifth season of eligibility in the 2026-27 school year in Kentucky. And while players have had their state court efforts upheld — or at least not yet overturned — the players who filed suit in Kentucky are now ineligible. No. 12 Texas Tech plays at Colorado on Saturday.

Friday's ruling is another sign of how haphazard and chaotic the NCAA's attempted implementation of its five-for-five rule has been. Over the summer, the NCAA announced that all players would have five school years to play five seasons starting with the 2026-27 athletic seasons. However, players who had played their fourth season in four school years in 2025-26 were not given a fifth year of eligibility.

The August suit involved 38 players, including former North Carolina basketball player Seth Trimble and former Missouri basketball player Mark Mitchell, along with Castellanos. Mitchell and Trimble, too, are ineligible. But their seasons haven't started yet. Mitchell was set to go to Kentucky before returning to Missouri. Trimble transferred to Louisville.

Kentucky linebacker Alex Afari is also among the players who are suddenly ineligible. Afari has 11 tackles through four games so far this season.

Castellanos was a late addition to Texas Tech's roster and has appeared in four games for the Red Raiders and attempted four passes as a backup to Will Hammond that went for 35 yards and two touchdowns in special play packages. He also threw an interception on the opening play of the Red Raiders' Week 3 win over Houston. He has rushed 10 times for 44 yards and two scores.

Before joining Texas Tech, Castellanos spent his freshman season at UCF. He played five games for the Knights before transferring to Boston College. He was the Eagles' starting QB in 2023 and for the start of the 2024 season before he was moved to the bench. He transferred to Florida State in 2025, where he was the Seminoles' starter and threw for over 2,700 yards, rushed for over 550 yards and had 24 total touchdowns.

articles.title: Man City guilty charges: Which clubs did 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?
articles.summary: BBC Sport follows the trail of transfer money flowing to other clubs during Manchester City's period of financial rule-breaking.
articles.body:
The money flowed around football. It made a lot of other clubs richer. It helped teams everywhere and especially in the Premier League.

These have been some of the arguments used by those backing Manchester City in the media and online since the verdicts declaring the club guilty came in and an appeal was announced. The suggestion is that there was a net benefit to the game as a whole, and in particular the clubs to whom Manchester City paid big transfer fees.

The more than £900m by which the independent commission found the club had "inflated" its accounts was not all spent on transfer fees.

Clubs have many bills, including wages for players and other staff, utilities, insurance, infrastructure costs, commercial fees and much more.

But the roughly £1.2bn Man City spent on players between 2009-2018 (about £900m net spend) was more than anybody else in that period.

That outlay was vital in making them England's most successful club, and would surely have been heavily reduced had they not knowingly broken the rules, as the independent commission concluded.

So where did City's money flow to in the transfer market, and what impact did it have?

Man City confirm appeal against guilty verdict

Man City whistleblower to lose witness protection

Who did Man City pay most money to between 2009 and 2018?

The amount required to sign the player is the most obvious, but there are also agents fees, legal expenses, administration money and potentially signing-on bonuses.

That means the money dished out by Manchester City during the 'asterisk era' will have reached people and bodies who work in the background of football deal-making and is difficult to track.

But what can be done is analysis of the fundamental interactions between City and other clubs.

Below is a list of every club to whom Manchester City paid transfer fees between summer 2009 and winter 2018, in descending order from the most money to the least.

The list is for senior players and does not include free transfers, loans or academy graduates.

That is 46 different clubs in 19 national league systems.

For some of them, the fees paid by City were the highest the clubs had ever received at the time.

Looking at the spread of money among clubs demonstrates just how far and wide Manchester City 's money was spent.

The split in money spent on transfer fees by City during the timeframe is relatively even across some of the highest-ranked leagues in Europe, though the Premier League is higher than any other.

Just over a quarter of their total transfer outlay was paid to clubs in the English top flight.

They signed players from eight Premier League clubs, and the same amount in La Liga.

A combined £13m was spent on two players in the Championship.

Manchester City 's spending power unquestionably changed the world football transfer market - their willingness to pay higher fees and wages meant prices rose for everybody else too.

And once the world knows that a club has a wedge of cash burning a hole in its pocket courtesy of City, it can be difficult to spend it.

Asking prices may rise, and having an influx of money is no guarantee of it being well spent.

For many of the teams to whom City paid the most during this time, the money did not work out particularly beneficially.

Let's take a look at some of the more interesting cases.

First up, Wolfsburg. They immediately signed winger Julian Draxler for about half the fee received for Kevin de Bruyne in 2016, as well as others including veteran defender Dante.

Having lost De Bruyne, they dropped from second to eighth in the Bundesliga before narrowly avoiding relegation in the subsequent two seasons.

And things did not go particularly well for second highest-ranked club Monaco either.

The most direct replacements they signed following the sales of Benjamin Mendy and Bernardo Silva in the same summer to Manchester City - Terence Kongolo and Keita Balde - did not work out in the long run, and the team went from winning Ligue 1 and reaching the Champions League semi-finals to almost being relegated within two years.

The club City purchased most players from in the 2009-18 period - Arsenal (four) - did not mount a serious Premier League title challenge during that time.

Some clubs who did not receive payments from City could also argue that the spending of money from their "inflated" accounts compromised their chances.

For example, Manchester City paid very similar totals to Benfica and Porto during the era, but nothing to Sporting, the club which makes up the big three in Portugal.

Sporting did not win a title between 2009 and 2018. There are many reasons for that, but could one of them be the fact that their direct rivals received money from City that would perhaps not have been on offer had they followed football's financial rules?

What does Man City guilty verdict mean for their squad?

HMRC urged to scrutinise tax implications of Man City case

Man City not 'above the rules', says No 10 after backlash to Burnham remarks

There are also some ancillary fees which reached clubs whom Manchester City did not deal with directly.

Some players were subject to sell-on clauses, where the club City where buying the player from owed money to the previous team who owned the player.

For example, Queens Park Rangers earned roughly £9m from Raheem Sterling's move to City from Liverpool in 2015.

Barnsley took about £7m of the transfer fee paid to Everton for John Stones in 2016, and the Toffees also had to pass on about £2.5m to Wolves when Joleon Lescott moved to Manchester in 2009.

The Sterling and Stones clauses were worth more than most players operating in the English Football League at that time, significantly strengthening the financial positions of QPR and Barnsley.

To this day Barnsley have not sold a player for a higher amount than the fee they are believed to have received for Stones.

But QPR have not returned to the Premier League and Barnsley dropped down to League One from the Championship after two seasons.

Manchester City 's spending during the time in which they were breaking the rules certainly had an enormous impact, on their own upward trajectory, the futures of other clubs around the world and the wider football economy.

But the reality is that it is impossible to unweave the tapestry of football history during that time and since - too much has happened and there are too many indirect consequences.

The effects of that spending will reverberate for years to come.

articles.title: Tyler Adams Named USMNT Captain by Mauricio Pochettino After Tim Ream's International Retirement
articles.summary: United States men's national soccer team head coach Mauricio Pochettino has named midfielder Tyler Adams as the new captain after ex-captain and center back Tim Ream announced his international retirement.
articles.body:
United States men's national soccer team head coach Mauricio Pochettino has named midfielder Tyler Adams as the new captain after ex-captain and center back Tim Ream announced his international retirement .

The 27-year-old Adams, who also plays for Bournemouth, has made 60 lifetime appearances for the United States dating back to 2017.

Adams previously captained the United States squad at the 2022 FIFA World Cup, leading the Americans out of the group stage and into the Round of 16. Last May, Pochettino announced Ream as the team's captain for this year's World Cup. The Americans won their group and beat Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Round of 32 before losing to Belgium.

At the club level, Adams began his career with New York Red Bulls before moving to RB Leipzig in 2019. He left there in 2022 for a season with Leeds United before signing a five-year deal with Bournemouth in 2023. Adams helped the team finish sixth in the Premier League table last year.

Currently, the USMNT is playing a run of international friendlies. They recently beat Peru 4-1 and Chile 4-2 and will now face Mexico on Saturday and Canada on Tuesday.

articles.title: USMNT Readies for Duel in the Desert vs. Mexico
articles.summary: TEMPE, Ariz. – There are a lot of things to say about U.S. versus Mexico, a classic series that dates back more than 90 years since the first all-time meetin...
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. – There are a lot of things to say about U.S. versus Mexico, a classic series that dates back more than 90 years since the first all-time meeting in 1934, but one point that players on the U.S. Men's National Team are conveying right now is that they expect the latest edition to live up to the rivalry tag.

"Dislike, hate. I mean, it's a rivalry," midfielder Tyler Adams said. "However, you want to describe a rivalry. When you talk about rivalries, whether it's in Europe in club football or whatever it is, there is a sense of always wanting to win and compete at the highest level. This is one of those games. It's gone on for a long time. There's a lot of history there, and history creates that rivalry, of course, but you just want that winning advantage. Anything you can do to win."

"Mexico is the biggest game for us," midfielder Gio Reyna said. "It's been circled on this window more than any game."

The USMNT meets Mexico for the 80th time on Saturday, Oct. 3 in Glendale, Ariz. The "Duel in the Desert" kicks off at 7:00 p.m. MT at State Farm Stadium, which is home to the NFL's Arizona Cardinals and can expand to seat approximately 73,000.

"It's going to be like a little war on the field," wingback Sergiño Dest said. "These are the toughest games, and you will feel it. The atmosphere is going to be amazing."

Saturday's matchup is the first time the two 2026 FIFA World Cup co-hosts have faced each other since last summer in the Concacaf Gold Cup Final. A young and relatively inexperienced U.S. side under Mauricio Pochettino in his first year as head coach fought bravely but fell short 2-1 at NRG Stadium in Houston as Mexico secured back-to-back Gold Cup titles.

The atmosphere for that Final was deemed World Cup-level, and with the October matchup hosted at an NFL stadium of a comparable capacity, the environment is expected to be just as loud and passionate.

"These games, I feel like it's the real culture and the real passion of football," Dest said. "Rivalries between teams in general are always amazing to see… playing with America against Mexico is one of the best games here. It's going to be a tough game."

"Ever since I first played against Mexico, it's always been the same," fullback Antonee Robinson said. "It doesn't matter whether it's a qualifier, an international match, Nations League, Gold Cup – it's always a fierce competition. You want to win, and it feels really personal."

Six players on Pochettino's current roster saw the field for that Gold Cup Final last summer, including the lone goal scorer for the USMNT that day, center back Chris Richards, and the man who assisted him, midfielder Sebastian Berhalter. The pair plus 11 more holdovers from the USMNT that won Group D to advance to the knockout stage of this summer's World Cup have been telling the 13 first-time call-ups in fall camp what to expect with a rivalry match in front of them.

"That it's never friendly and that it's going to be a fun game," Berhalter on what he told the younger players about Mexico. "It's great for them to see that and hopefully compete and add because we need them. It's going to be a great game."

"I'd rather you go into a tackle and run everywhere and get around the ball and be feisty and have a little tenacity to your game than sit back and watch the game go by," Adams said. "So, all these players that have the opportunity to play tomorrow, that's what we need from them."

For players like 18-year-old forward Julian Hall, who made program history by becoming the youngest player to score a goal in each of his two caps, it's an opportunity to see the rivalry for the first time up close and in person.

"I'm expecting a dogfight," Hall said. "I've watched a lot of them in the past, and I'm excited to see what it's like – the environment, the experience. Hopefully, we come out with a win."

The U.S. will be looking to extend its winning record over Mexico since 2021. The U.S. holds a 5W-2L-2D advantage in the series, including victories in the 2021 and 2024 editions of the Concacaf Nations League Finals as well as the 2021 Gold Cup championship match.

In the latest edition, the U.S. will also aim to continue its current run of form in a new era under Pochettino, which has gotten off to a winning start. The group is coming off back-to-back wins over Peru in Orlando, Fla. on Sept. 26 and Chile in St. Louis, Mo. on Sept. 29 to kick off the four-match fall window. So far, the team has scored four goals in each victory with a variety of contributions from players all over the pitch.

Like the U.S., Mexico is coming off a Round of 16 appearance in FIFA World Cup 2026. After winning Group A without conceding a goal, Mexico's run came to an end in a classic match against tournament semifinalist England at Estadio Azteca.

Since then, Mexico has introduced a new head coach, Rafael Márquez, to succeed the retired Javier Aguirre. One of the most legendary defenders in Mexican soccer history, Márquez is a five-time World Cup participant. His playing resume is stacked with trophies, including four La Liga titles. In 2006 as a member of FC Barcelona, he became the first Mexican player to win the UEFA Champions League. He, like Pochettino, has been signed with his Federation through 2030.

Upon his arrival, Márquez vowed to take Mexico "to another level." Two matches into his debut as manager, Mexico is unbeaten but still looking for its first win after a pair of 1-1 draws against Peru and Colombia in September.

Since the previous meeting last summer between the two senior National Teams, the two countries also met for a youth-level championship. Mexico defeated the U-19 U.S. Men's National Team to capture the 2026 Concacaf U-20 Men's Championship at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City on Aug. 9, 2026, Mexico's second consecutive title.

"Mexico, in the last year, went in a great direction," Reyna said. "A lot of good, young players coming through as well. So, it's not the easiest game."

For some of the younger players on the USMNT roster, there may be some nerves heading into Saturday's match. Hosting a rival in front of a large crowd is an intense atmosphere, but the message that veterans are delivering to these players has been clear: we are going to need you.

"We need that courage. We need that bravery. We need them to be fearless like they are, so that they can have an impact," Adams said.

"The only thing I can help them with is to stay calm and believe in all the abilities they trained for all these years and show what you got because that's what we need," Dest said.

Dest knows well what it's like to play in USA-Mexico matches in the desert. The wingback started the Concacaf Nations League Semifinal match between the two sides in 2023 at Allegiant Stadium. On a dominant night for the U.S., Dest assisted the third goal of the night to striker Ricardo Pepi as the U.S. defeated Mexico 3-0, giving the 25-year-old both respect for a tough opponent and a taste of what it takes to defeat a longstanding rival.

"Mexico is always going to be a tough opponent," Dest said. "They're always aggressive, and they want to win. And so do we. So it's going to be a difficult game for both sides, and may the best win."
